explanation: In a galvanic (voltaic) cell a spontaneous redox reaction (dG < 0, E°cell > 0) pushes electrons through an external wire from the anode to the cathode. Oxidation happens at the anode (electrons released, M → Mⁿ⁺ + n e⁻), reduction at the cathode (Mⁿ⁺ + n e⁻ → M); in a galvanic cell the anode is the negative terminal and the cathode is positive. The salt bridge completes the circuit by letting ions migrate — cations toward the cathode, anions toward the anode — so neither beaker builds up net charge. On the AP exam you must label anode/cathode, state oxidation vs reduction, and give the directions of both electron flow (in the wire) and ion flow (in the bridge), all of which this animation shows live.
bullets: Yellow electrons travel anode → cathode through the external wire.
Anode = oxidation (− terminal); cathode = reduction (+ terminal).
Salt bridge: cations move to cathode, anions to anode.
Mnemonic: AN-OX, RED-CAT (anode oxidation, reduction cathode).
